documents.t: useConfig provides read-only access to the current user configuration for ascii-ui. It returns a deep copy of the global user config so that components can safely read values without mutating shared state. local config = ui.hooks.useConfig()

Call useConfig at the top level of a component to retrieve the current ascii-ui user configuration. The returned value is a deep copy, ensuring that components cannot mutate the global config accidentally. local config = ui.hooks.useConfig() print(config.characters.right_triangule) Use this hook whenever you need to read user preferences, theme settings, or character overrides defined in the ascii-ui configuration.
useConfig does not take any parameters. It always returns the current user configuration from the global ascii-ui settings.

useConfig returns a deep copy of the current ascii-ui user configuration. Name Type Description config ascii-ui.Config A deep copy of the global user configuration. It is read-only — modifying it will not affect the actual user config. Use it to safely access character overrides, keymaps, or log level.

Use useConfig to access user-defined characters or symbols from the global config: local ui = require("ascii-ui") local useConfig = ui.hooks.useConfig local Paragraph = ui.components.Paragraph local CharacterInfo = ui.createComponent("CharacterInfo", function() local config = useConfig() return { Paragraph({ content = "Right triangle character: " .. config.characters.right_triangule }), } end) return CharacterInfo

ui.mount starts the render loop for a root component. It performs the initial render, opens the viewport, binds keyboard interactions, and starts listening for state changes. ui.mount(RootComponent) -- or with an explicit viewport: ui.mount(RootComponent, viewport)

Parameters​ Name Type Required Description RootComponent FunctionalComponent Yes The root component to render. This is a component created with ui.createComponent. viewport ascii-ui.Viewport No Where to render the UI. Defaults to a centered Neovim floating window. Returns​ Name Type Description bufnr integer The Neovim buffer number used by the viewport. Returns -1 for non-Neovim viewports (e.g. StdoutViewport).

The simplest call opens a centered, rounded floating window automatically sized to fit the rendered content: local ui = require("ascii-ui") local MyApp = ui.createComponent("MyApp", function() return { ui.components.Paragraph({ content = "Hello from a floating window!" }), } end) ui.mount(MyApp)

Pass a StdoutViewport to render to the terminal instead of a Neovim window. Useful for headless scripts, CI pipelines, or animations: local ui = require("ascii-ui") local MyApp = ui.createComponent("MyApp", function() return { ui.components.Paragraph({ content = "Rendered to stdout!" }), } end) ui.mount(MyApp, ui.viewports.StdoutViewport.new())

ui.mount manages the full lifecycle of the UI: Initial render — Calls fiber.render(RootComponent) to build the fiber tree and produce the first buffer. Open viewport — Calls viewport:open(). For the default floating window this creates the Neovim buffer and window. Update viewport — Calls viewport:update(buffer) to write the rendered content. Keyboard bindings — Registers vim.on_key for h/j/k/l navigation between focusable segments. State change listener — On every useState setter call, rerenders and refreshes the viewport. Cleanup — On WinClosed, detaches all bindings, calls root:unmount() to clean up effects and timers, calls viewport:close(), and runs useEffect cleanups.
When a component throws an error during render, ascii-ui catches it and displays a formatted error message in the viewport instead of crashing silently.

If your component throws during the initial render or a re-render, you'll see an error screen: ═══ RENDER ERROR ═══ Type: render Component: MyApp > Counter Message: attempt to index local 'state' (a nil value) Hint: Components must return a list (table) of FiberNode or BufferLine objects. Did you forget to wrap your return value? Example: return { Segment:new({ content = "hello" }):wrap() } ═══════════════════

ascii-ui categorizes errors by type: Type Description render Error during component render hook Error in a hook (useState, useEffect, etc.) effect Error in an effect or cleanup function interaction Error in user interaction handler viewport Error in viewport operations Each error type includes a contextual hint to help you debug the issue.

After a render error, the viewport remains open showing the error message. Fix the issue in your component code, and the error will disappear on the next successful render. See Error Handling for more details on debugging and common error patterns.

These bindings are active while the ascii-ui window is focused: Key Action h Move focus left / to the previous focusable element l Move focus right / to the next focusable element k Move focus up j Move focus down <CR> Trigger the SELECT interaction on the focused element q Close the window (configurable via ui.setup)

Any object satisfying the ascii-ui.Viewport interface can be passed as the second argument. The interface requires these methods: Method Description open() Initialize/open the output target close() Tear down update(buffer) Render the buffer frame is_focused() Returns true if the viewport has user focus enable_edits() Allow text input (for Input widgets) disable_edits() Revert to read-only get_id() Neovim window id, or -1 get_bufnr() Neovim buffer number, or -1 get_ns_id() Neovim namespace id, or -1 See the StdoutViewport documentation for a built-in example.

Imagine a new kind of application that lives inside Neovim — not just a plugin that adds a feature here and there, but a fully-formed, interactive experience. A Neovim App is exactly that: a self-contained application that runs inside your editor, renders its own UI using ASCII characters, and reacts to user input in real time. Unlike traditional plugins, a Neovim App is designed to feel like its own world. You can launch it from the command line, from another plugin, or as part of your workflow. In short: a Neovim App isn't just extending Neovim — it's building on top of it. It's a new way to think about what's possible inside your editor.

Every ascii-ui.nvim application has the same three parts: 1. Setup (optional) → ui.setup({ ... }) configure theme, keymaps, log level 2. Root component → ui.createComponent declare what to render 3. Mount → ui.mount(App) open the window and start the loop local ui = require("ascii-ui") -- Optional: global configuration ui.setup({}) -- Root component: the top of your UI tree local App = ui.createComponent("App", function() return ui.components.Paragraph({ content = "Hello from a Neovim App!" }) end) -- Mount: opens a floating window and starts the reactive loop ui.mount(App)

When you call ui.mount(App): ascii-ui renders the component tree into an in-memory Buffer. A floating window (or any custom viewport) is opened and filled with the rendered content. The framework listens for state changes. When a hook like useState updates, the tree is re-rendered and the window is refreshed automatically. Built-in keybindings (h, j, k, l) let the cursor move between interactive segments (buttons, inputs, selects). When the window is closed, all effects are cleaned up and the event loop stops.

You can run a Neovim App headlessly from the terminal without a full editor UI: # Run inside a Neovim floating window nvim -c "luafile my_app.lua" # Run with stdout rendering (no window, outputs ANSI to terminal) nvim --headless -c "luafile my_app.lua" For stdout rendering, use ui.viewports.StdoutViewport: local ui = require("ascii-ui") local StdoutViewport = ui.viewports.StdoutViewport local App = ui.createComponent("App", function() return ui.components.Paragraph({ content = "Hello from stdout!" }) end) ui.mount(App, StdoutViewport.new())

ascii-ui provides a testing library inspired by React Testing Library to help you test your components. The library provides user-centric queries and assertions that focus on what the user sees and interacts with.

The testing library has two modes: Unit Testing (require("ascii-ui.testing")) — Test components in isolation without a Neovim window E2E Testing (require("ascii-ui.testing.e2e")) — Test components in a real Neovim window with keyboard interactions
The testing library is included with ascii-ui: local testing = require("ascii-ui.testing") local testing_e2e = require("ascii-ui.testing.e2e")

Unit tests are faster and don't require a Neovim window. Use them for most component testing. E2E tests are slower but test real keyboard interactions, cursor movement, and buffer behavior. Use them when you need to verify actual user interactions. See the detailed guides: Unit Testing — Fast, isolated component tests E2E Testing — Full integration tests with keyboard interactions

Prefer unit tests — Use testing.render() for most tests. They're faster and don't require a Neovim window. Use E2E for interactions — Use testing_e2e.mount() when testing keyboard navigation, cursor movement, or real buffer behavior. Query like a user — Use getByText() to find elements the way a user would see them, not by internal IDs. Use waitForText for async — When testing state changes or async operations, use waitForText() instead of bufferContains(). Assert on output, not implementation — Test what the user sees (hasLines), not internal state.
Use E2E testing when you need to test keyboard interactions, cursor movement, or real Neovim buffer behavior.

local testing_e2e = require("ascii-ui.testing.e2e") local ui = require("ascii-ui") local Select = ui.components.Select local it = require("plenary.async.tests").it describe("MyComponent E2E", function() it("navigates with keyboard", function() local App = ui.createComponent("Test", function() return Select({ options = { "a", "b", "c" } }) end) local screen = testing_e2e.mount(App) -- Wait for initial render assert(screen:waitForText("[x] a")) -- Simulate keypress screen:press("j") -- Assert cursor moved assert(screen:cursorIsAt(2)) -- Clean up timers and close window screen:unmount() end) end)
local screen = testing_e2e.mount(Component) The mount() function opens a real Neovim window and returns an E2EScreen object.

Unmounts the component and closes the window. This cleans up timers and prevents leaks. screen:unmount() Call this after each test to ensure proper cleanup, especially when testing components with useTimeout or useInterval.
Checks if the Neovim buffer contains the given text. assert(screen:bufferContains("hello"))
Waits for text to appear in the buffer (useful for async operations). assert(screen:waitForText("loading...", 2000))
Asserts the cursor is at the given position. assert(screen:cursorIsAt(2, 5))
Simulates a Neovim keypress. screen:press("j") -- move down screen:press("<CR>") -- press Enter screen:press("lll") -- move right 3 times
E2EScreen inherits all methods from Screen, so you can use the same queries and assertions: screen:hasText("hello") screen:hasLine("[x] apple") screen:toLines()
If you have existing tests with duplicated helpers, you can migrate to the testing library:

local function feed(keys) vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(keys, "mtx", true) end local function buffer_contains(bufnr, pattern) return vim.wait(1000, function() local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, false) local content_str = vim.iter(lines):join("\n") return string.find(content_str, pattern, 1, true) ~= nil end) end describe("MyComponent", function() it("works", function() local bufnr = ui.mount(App) assert(buffer_contains(bufnr, "hello")) feed("j") assert(buffer_contains(bufnr, "world")) end) end)

local testing_e2e = require("ascii-ui.testing.e2e") describe("MyComponent", function() it("works", function() local screen = testing_e2e.mount(App) assert(screen:waitForText("hello")) screen:press("j") assert(screen:waitForText("world")) screen:unmount() end) end)
Use unit testing to test components in isolation. This is faster and doesn't require a Neovim window.

local testing = require("ascii-ui.testing") local ui = require("ascii-ui") local Select = ui.components.Select describe("MyComponent", function() it("renders options", function() local App = ui.createComponent("Test", function() return Select({ options = { "apple", "banana", "cherry" } }) end) local screen = testing.render(App) -- Assert the rendered output assert(screen:hasLines({ "[x] apple", "[ ] banana", "[ ] cherry" })) end) end)
local screen = testing.render(Component) The render() function takes a component and returns a Screen object with query and assertion methods.
Queries find segments in the rendered buffer. They throw an error if the element is not found (except queryByText which returns nil).
Finds a segment containing the given text. local segment = screen:getByText("apple") assert(segment.content == "apple")
Like getByText, but returns nil instead of throwing an error. local segment = screen:queryByText("missing") assert(segment == nil)
Finds all segments containing the given text. local segments = screen:getAllByText("item") assert(#segments == 3)
Finds a segment with the given highlight group. local segment = screen:getByHighlight("Selection")
Returns the first focusable segment. local focusable = screen:getFocusable() assert(focusable:is_focusable())
Returns all focusable segments. local focusables = screen:getAllFocusable() assert(#focusables == 3)
Assertions check properties of the rendered buffer.
Checks if the buffer contains the given text anywhere. assert(screen:hasText("hello"))
Checks if the buffer contains an exact line. assert(screen:hasLine("[x] apple"))
Checks if the buffer exactly matches the given lines. assert(screen:hasLines({ "[x] apple", "[ ] banana" }))
Checks if a focusable segment with the given text exists. assert(screen:hasFocusable("Submit"))
Checks if a segment with the given highlight exists. assert(screen:hasHighlight("Selection"))
Triggers the SELECT interaction on a segment and re-renders. screen:select("apple") assert(screen:hasLine("[x] apple"))
Triggers a custom interaction on a segment and re-renders. local interaction_type = require("ascii-ui.interaction_type") screen:trigger("button", interaction_type.SELECT)
Moves focus to a focusable segment (unit test mode). screen:focus("Submit")
Returns the buffer as an array of lines. local lines = screen:toLines() -- { "[x] apple", "[ ] banana" }
Returns the buffer as a single string. local snapshot = screen:toSnapshot() -- "[x] apple\n[ ] banana"

StdoutViewport is a viewport implementation that renders the UI to terminal stdout using ANSI truecolor escape codes. It is useful for headless scripts, CI pipelines, terminal animations, or any context where Neovim's windowing API is not available. local viewport = ui.viewports.StdoutViewport.new() ui.mount(MyComponent, viewport)

Creates a new StdoutViewport. Parameters​ Name Type Required Description writer fun(s: string) No A custom output function. Defaults to io.write. Override this in tests or to redirect output to a file or buffer. Returns​ A new StdoutViewport instance that satisfies the ascii-ui.Viewport interface.

local ui = require("ascii-ui") local MyApp = ui.createComponent("MyApp", function() return { ui.components.Paragraph({ content = "Hello from stdout!" }), } end) ui.mount(MyApp, ui.viewports.StdoutViewport.new())

StdoutViewport works with all hooks, including useInterval for animations: local ui = require("ascii-ui") local useState = ui.hooks.useState local useInterval = ui.hooks.useInterval local Paragraph = ui.components.Paragraph local Clock = ui.createComponent("Clock", function() local tick, setTick = useState(0) useInterval(function() setTick(tick + 1) end, 1000) return { Paragraph({ content = "Tick: " .. tick }), } end) ui.mount(Clock, ui.viewports.StdoutViewport.new()) Each second the screen clears and rerenders with the updated tick count.

Segments with a color field are rendered with ANSI truecolor sequences: local ui = require("ascii-ui") local Segment = ui.blocks.Segment local Bufferline = ui.blocks.Bufferline local ColorDemo = ui.createComponent("ColorDemo", function() return { Bufferline( Segment({ content = "Red text", color = { fg = "#ff0000" } }), Segment({ content = " | " }), Segment({ content = "Blue bg", color = { bg = "#0000ff" } }) ), } end) ui.mount(ColorDemo, ui.viewports.StdoutViewport.new())
local lines = {} local viewport = ui.viewports.StdoutViewport.new(function(s) table.insert(lines, s) end) ui.mount(MyApp, viewport) -- lines now contains the rendered output

documents.t: Feature Support Color (truecolor) Supported via ANSI SGR escape codes Keyboard interactions Not supported (is_focused() always returns false) Input widget edits Not applicable WinClosed cleanup Not triggered (no Neovim window) get_id() / get_bufnr() / get_ns_id() Always return -1

On each update(buffer) call, StdoutViewport: Clears the terminal (ESC[H ESC[2J). Iterates all buffer lines. For each colored segment, wraps the text with ANSI SGR truecolor sequences (ESC[38;2;r;g;bm for foreground, ESC[48;2;r;g;bm for background) followed by a reset (ESC[0m). Writes all lines separated by newlines.
